limitations: Forced paced completed offscreen work, not native presentation or input latency.
All-thread process CPU counters have finite Windows resolution; zero does not prove zero work.
Costs need not add across isolated/combined cases because worker scheduling, batching and warmed state differ.
Opaque-fill omission and UI-only native freezing change pixels and are diagnostic, not accepted optimizations.
The opaque-fill omission includes ordinary meshes beyond the palette; it does not alone prove that a palette-only change wins.
One shared-host observation per case; no precise external-CPU attribution or statistical qualification.
Source/binary identities are preserved separately from later production or documentation changes.
